title: What Is Lost in Translation
sentences: Every translator is caught in a quiet dilemma between fidelity to the original and readability in the new language.
Har bir tarjimon asl matnga sodiqlik va yangi tildagi o'qishlilik o'rtasidagi jimjit ikkilanishda qoladi.
Words rarely map neatly onto one another; each carries a web of connotations shaped by history and culture.
So'zlar kamdan-kam hollarda bir-biriga aniq mos keladi; har biri tarix va madaniyat shakllantirgan ma'nolar to'rini olib yuradi.
So-called untranslatable words, such as the Portuguese saudade, are often cited to illustrate the point.
Portugalcha saudade kabi tarjima qilib bo'lmaydigan deb ataladigan so'zlar bu fikrni ko'rsatish uchun tez-tez keltiriladi.
Yet the problem is less about individual words than about rhythm, humour and the unspoken assumptions of a text.
Biroq muammo alohida so'zlardan ko'ra matnning ritmi, hazili va aytilmagan farazlari bilan bog'liq.
A joke that relies on wordplay, for instance, can rarely be rescued without being rebuilt from scratch.
Masalan, so'z o'yiniga asoslangan hazilni noldan qayta qurmasdan saqlab qolish kamdan-kam mumkin.
Inevitably, something is lost, but skilled translators also find ways to convey nuance that a literal version would miss.
Muqarrar ravishda nimadir yo'qoladi, ammo mohir tarjimonlar so'zma-so'z tarjima e'tibordan chetda qoldiradigan nozik ma'nolarni yetkazish yo'llarini ham topadi.
In that sense, a great translation is not a copy but a performance, as much an act of interpretation as of transfer.
Shu ma'noda buyuk tarjima nusxa emas, balki ijro bo'lib, u ko'chirish qanchalik bo'lsa, talqin ham shunchalik.

title: The Unreliable Archive of Memory
sentences: We tend to imagine memory as a faithful archive, a vault in which experiences are stored intact.
Biz xotirani tajribalar buzilmasdan saqlanadigan ishonchli arxiv, xazina deb tasavvur qilishga moyilmiz.
In reality, each act of remembering involves reconstructing the past, and every reconstruction leaves the memory subtly altered.
Aslida har bir eslash o'tmishni qayta qurishni o'z ichiga oladi va har bir qayta qurish xotirani sezilmas darajada o'zgartiradi.
Experiments have shown that people can be led to recall, in vivid detail, events that never took place.
Tajribalar odamlarni hech qachon bo'lmagan voqealarni yorqin tafsilotlari bilan eslashga undash mumkinligini ko'rsatgan.
Even emotionally intense memories, which feel unshakeably accurate, are susceptible to distortion.
Hatto mutlaqo aniq tuyuladigan hissiy jihatdan kuchli xotiralar ham buzilishga moyil.
This has sobering implications for the courtroom, where eyewitness testimony has long been treated as compelling evidence.
Bu guvohlar ko'rsatmasi uzoq vaqt ishonchli dalil sifatida qabul qilinib kelgan sud zali uchun jiddiy xulosalarga olib keladi.
Numerous wrongful convictions have later been overturned once other evidence came to light.
Boshqa dalillar oshkor bo'lgach, ko'plab noto'g'ri hukmlar keyinchalik bekor qilingan.
None of this means that memory is worthless; rather, it reminds us that confidence and accuracy are not the same thing.
Bularning hech biri xotira qadrsiz degani emas; aksincha, u bizga ishonch va aniqlik bir narsa emasligini eslatadi.

title: The Paradox of Progress
sentences: By almost any measurable standard, humanity has never been better off.
Deyarli har qanday o'lchanadigan mezon bo'yicha insoniyat hech qachon bunchalik farovon bo'lmagan.
Life expectancy, literacy and material prosperity have risen to unprecedented levels in a remarkably short time.
Umr davomiyligi, savodxonlik va moddiy farovonlik hayratlanarli qisqa vaqtda misli ko'rilmagan darajaga ko'tarildi.
And yet surveys in many wealthy countries reveal persistent, and in some cases growing, discontent.
Shunga qaramay, ko'plab boy mamlakatlardagi so'rovnomalar doimiy, ba'zi hollarda esa o'sib borayotgan norozilikni ko'rsatmoqda.
Economists have long puzzled over this paradox.
Iqtisodchilar uzoq vaqtdan beri bu paradoks ustida bosh qotirib kelishadi.
One explanation is that our aspirations rise as quickly as our circumstances improve, so the gap between what we have and what we want never closes.
Bir izohga ko'ra, sharoitimiz yaxshilangani sari intilishlarimiz ham shunchalik tez o'sadi, shuning uchun bor narsamiz va xohlaganimiz orasidagi farq hech qachon yopilmaydi.
Another is that we judge our wellbeing relative to those around us rather than in absolute terms.
Boshqa izohga ko'ra, biz farovonligimizni mutlaq o'lchovda emas, atrofimizdagilarga nisbatan baholaymiz.
If either is true, then contentment may depend less on further growth than on how we choose to measure a good life.
Agar ulardan biri to'g'ri bo'lsa, qanoat keyingi o'sishdan ko'ra yaxshi hayotni qanday o'lchashni tanlashimizga ko'proq bog'liq bo'lishi mumkin.

title: The Silk Road Reconsidered
sentences: The term Silk Road conjures up images of long caravans carrying precious fabric from China to Rome.
Ipak yo'li atamasi Xitoydan Rimga qimmatbaho mato tashigan uzun karvonlar tasvirini yodga soladi.
This is, however, something of a misconception.
Biroq bu qandaydir noto'g'ri tasavvurdir.
There was never a single road, but rather a shifting network of routes along which goods changed hands many times.
Hech qachon yagona yo'l bo'lmagan, aksincha, tovarlar ko'p marta qo'ldan qo'lga o'tgan o'zgaruvchan yo'llar tarmog'i bo'lgan.
Few merchants travelled the entire distance; instead, local intermediaries, many of them Sogdians, dominated the trade.
Kamdan-kam savdogarlar butun masofani bosib o'tgan; buning o'rniga savdoda mahalliy vositachilar, ularning ko'pchiligi so'g'diylar hukmron bo'lgan.
Cities such as Samarkand and Bukhara flourished as hubs where languages, religions and technologies met.
Samarqand va Buxoro kabi shaharlar tillar, dinlar va texnologiyalar uchrashgan markazlar sifatida gullab-yashnagan.
Arguably, the most valuable cargo was not silk at all, but ideas: the dissemination of paper-making, mathematics and medicine.
Aytish mumkinki, eng qimmatli yuk umuman ipak emas, balki g'oyalar — qog'oz ishlab chiqarish, matematika va tibbiyotning tarqalishi edi.
Its legacy, therefore, lies less in trade figures than in its role as a conduit for the exchange of knowledge.
Shu sababli uning merosi savdo raqamlaridan ko'ra bilim almashinuvi kanali sifatidagi rolida namoyon bo'ladi.
